method: Opus 5 workflow annotator per PA from ffmpeg frame grabs; two independent verifier lenses per pitch (timing, scoreboard_identity) that both had to return and pass; then the Claude Code session built a review sheet per pitch (decision boundary frames, bug crops, continuity samples, release crops) and looked at it directly before marking a row verified.
limitations: Selected-frame AI review, not continuous playback or independent human inter-rater measurement. Release estimates have +/-0.15 s manual uncertainty. Same-game development data, not an independent benchmark.
starting_commit_meaning: Claim commit before PA27-32 (4th inning) annotation; candidates were created during this task.

issues: Motion start is wrong. At 3000.25 s Megill's left (stride) foot is clearly off the dirt with the knee raised, so the leg lift is already under way (raw frame vT30_2a_3000.25.jpg and the enlarged pitcher crop). He is still set with the glove at his chest and both feet planted at 2999.50, 2999.75 and 3000.00. The first sampled frame with the leg lift is therefore 3000.25, not 3000.50. The claimed continuity sample at 3000.25 ('pitcher on the rubber, still set at 3000.25') is false, which triggers refutation criterion (c).

Condition (3) is borderline at 2994.00. Urshela is upright in the box, but the bat is lowered across his hip with the barrel pointing down, and his head is tilted down toward his hands while he adjusts his gloves. Lesson (c) treats that as a fail. From 2994.25 his hands are raised to his chest with the bat up and his face turned to the pitcher (the same at 2994.50 and 2995.00). A conservative decision is 2994.25; 2994.00 is defensible only if the head-down, bat-lowered pose is read as facing the pitcher.

Condition (1) does fail before the decision, as claimed. 2993.50 and 2993.75 are the Urshela close-up with the '3B GIO URSHELA 0 FOR 1 STRIKEOUT' stat card, with no pitcher in frame. At 2994.00 the bug's second line is still drawing in (garbled '8. URSHELA'), but the main fields are readable.

The release is within tolerance and not refuted. At 3001.35 the throwing hand is cocked beside the head with the ball visible. At 3001.40 the arm is coming through at head height, motion-blurred. At 3001.45 the arm is extended forward toward the plate with the hand empty. At 3001.55 he is in follow-through. At 3001.25 he is still striding with the arm low and back. Release falls at about 3001.40-3001.45, inside 3001.40 +/- 0.15.

At 2994.00 the second bug line (batter banner) is still animating in: only the lower halves of '8. URSHELA' and '0-1' are drawn. It becomes fully readable at 2994.50 ('8. URSHELA 0-1'). The annotator's banner reading is correct, but at 2994.00 it is only a partial reading, confirmed by 2994.50.

Not refuting. At 2993.75 the shot is a close-up of Urshela with a '3B GIO URSHELA 0 FOR 1 STRIKEOUT' stat card (not live wide), so 2994.00 is the first live centre-field frame. That fits the claimed decision; the timing lens should confirm continuity to the motion start.

Note inaccuracy: the claim says Megill is 'side-on and set with the glove at his chest from about 2995.50'. In 2996.00, 2996.75 and 2997.25 he is actually squared to the plate, back to the camera with #38 visible and the glove at his chest (taking the sign). He is side-on and set only at 3000.00. This is descriptive only and does not change any time.

Between 2995.25 and 2996.00 Megill turns from side-on (feet together) to square: the free left foot moves out to widen his stance, while the pivot foot stays along the front edge of the rubber in the same spot. I read this as the turning that lesson (b) allows, not a step-off or a re-arrival. A stricter reading of 'foot off the dirt' could question it, but it is not a clear break.

Condition (3) at 2994.00 is borderline but defensible: Urshela's hands are low at his hip, the bat is lowered and his head is angled down toward his hands. Either way refutation (b) cannot apply, because 2993.75 is the home-plate close-up under the '3B GIO URSHELA 0 FOR 1 STRIKEOUT' stat card, with no pitcher in frame, so condition (1) fails there.

My own continuity samples leave a 2.75 s gap between 2997.25 and 3000.00 (my extra-frame budget was used on the feet check and the release bracket). Both endpoints are clean: live centre-field shot, pitcher on the rubber, batter in the box with the bat up, bug normal and not white.
